citations.text:
GPU Memory Hierarchy

Access Memory: Coalescing Packs Nearby Addresses into
Fewer Transactions





▪ Coalescing is evaluated for one warp memory instruction. Aligned, contiguous
  addresses touch fewer segments.
▪ Misalignment can cross extra boundaries. Strided accesses can touch many more
  segments.

result.answer: Coalescing for the contiguous global load; broadcast for the same-address shared load
result.hint: One mechanism packs nearby addresses into fewer transactions; the other lets identical addresses be served together.
result.explanation: Contiguous global addresses are packed into fewer transactions via coalescing, while same-address shared-memory reads can use broadcast rather than serializing bank conflicts.
